name: Open popup or new window
plain: Opens a new tab or popup window, but only right after a click or tap.
meaning: A site can put another page in front of the person (ads, login flows, payment pages). Popup blockers decide whether it happens, so it is the main way a site can steer attention to a second origin.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.persistence: Per window; users can allow pop-ups per site (Chrome Pop-ups and redirects setting, Firefox exceptions, Safari per-site setting)
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Needs sandbox allow-popups (and allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox for unsandboxed children)
steps: Handler calls window.open within about 5 s of the click
Browser opens window or shows blocked-popup icon

limits.headline: Can open a new tab or window, but only right after you tap or click
limits.user_action: You tap a link, a button, or Share, Print or Open in new tab.
can: Open a new tab or small window after a tap or click
Open a sign in window for a login or a payment
Open a link in a new tab you can close
cannot: Open a window with no tap or click, which browsers block by default
Open lots of windows from one tap in most cases
Control a window that belongs to a different site
Hide the address bar of the new window in modern browsers
limits.differs: iPhone Safari is a little stricter about which taps count.

story.what_it_is: After a click, a page can open a new tab or small window.
story.for_you: You click a link and a new tab opens, or you sign in with Google and a small window appears. Without a click, the browser blocks the pop up.
story.for_makers: Makers use pop ups for sign in windows, payment confirmations and help chats. The click rule exists because pop up ads were once everywhere.

use_cases.example: Clicking 'Sign in with Google' opens a small window to approve, then closes.
A PayPal button opens a small window to confirm payment, then returns you to the shop.
A shady ad site tries to open a new tab with every click anywhere on the page.
A browser game portal opens the leaderboard in a pop up.
A streamer's chat is popped out to a separate window so it can sit on a second monitor.
A bank opens a secure help chat in a small window.

technical_bounds: Blocked without transient user activation (Chrome, Safari, Firefox all block popups outside input handlers)
Transient activation lasts about 5 s in Chrome and Firefox (dom.user_activation.transient.timeout = 5000 ms); Safari uses a much shorter window (about 1 s)
window.open consumes the activation in Chrome and Safari, so a second popup in the same click is blocked
Firefox allows up to dom.popup_maximum (default 20) popups from one event
target=_blank and window.open imply noopener for links (Chrome 88, Firefox 79, Safari 12.1)
Popup features width and height are clamped to a minimum of 100 CSS px; position cannot be placed off screen

abuse: Phishing windows that mimic browser chrome

history.change: Popups opened from user clicks only; blocker icon in the address bar
Popups in cross-origin iframes limited; abusive redirect and popup interventions
Anchors with target=_blank get implicit rel=noopener
popup=true feature and window.open consumes transient activation across browsers (HTML spec)
